evidence_set: Twenty minutes after the injection, on haloperidol, the BPRS total was 33.4 (6.0) after placebo and 38.3 (7.1), 39.3 (5.0) and 45.3 (7.7) after 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5 mg/kg, significant at 0.3 (p = .005) and 0.5 mg/kg (p = .01), against baselines of 34.6 (7.0), 33.2 (4.2), 35.2 (5.4) and 36.9 (11.0); n = 9, 9, 9 and 7. The three psychosis items carried the change: 8.0 (3.1) after placebo against 9.8 (3.3) (p = .05), 9.3 (2.8) and 12.3 (2.5) (p = .02), from baselines of 8.1, 6.8, 6.6 and 6.9. At 90 and 180 minutes the total is at or below its own baseline in every condition (at 0.5 mg/kg, 32.3 and 32.3), while the psychosis score at 0.1 and 0.3 mg/kg is 7.0 at both times, just above baselines of 6.8 and 6.6, and Table 2 marks the 0.1 mg/kg value at 180 minutes significant although it sits below the placebo value of 7.9. The paper nowhere says whether the figures in brackets are standard deviations or standard errors; they make sense only as standard deviations. No test statistic, degrees of freedom, interval or effect size is printed.

The paper gives the timing of the later reports in three different ways: the abstract calls them delayed or prolonged effects at 8 to 24 hours, the results say the delusions came back about 6 to 8 hours after the injection, and the heading of the table that lists them per person reads 4 to 24 hours, while that table's own entries record delusions that lasted 12 hours in one person and were sustained over 12 hours in another, nightmares on two nights and visual hallucinations over several days. Nothing in the paper reconciles the three windows.

evidence_set: Free recall of a 12-word categorical list was lower on the ketamine day than on the salt-water day in 15 healthy volunteers: drug F1,14 = 9.63 (p = .008), time F4,56 = 5.16 (p = .005), drug x time F4,52 = 4.35 (p = .004); lower at 55 minutes F1,13 = 18.79 (p = .001) and at 90 minutes F1,13 = 6.25 (p = .026). Recognition of the same words (n = 14) was lower too: drug F1,13 = 17.48 (p = .001), time F4,52 = 6.05, drug x time F4,52 = 7.95 (p < .001), lower at 10 minutes F1,13 = 8.92 (p = .01) and 55 minutes F1,13 = 18.78. The attention score fell less markedly: drug x time F4,56 = 2.71 (p = .05), lower at 55 minutes only, F1,14 = 8.79 (p = .01). Only for attention does the paper say what its individual count measures: 9 of 15 people fell from their own pre-infusion level at 55 minutes of the ketamine infusion, which is not a comparison with the salt-water day; the next sentence gives 13 of 15 for free recall and 9 of 14 for recognition without restating the time or the reference. All three measures come from the same word list, so they are not independent of each other.

evidence_set: For the BPRS hallucinatory-behaviour item, which is one of the three items of the positive subscale, the authors used the original, wider item description so that perceptual distortions as well as hallucinations could be scored on it, so this study's positive-subscale scores are not directly comparable with studies that score that item more narrowly, and a rise on that item cannot be read as evidence of hallucinations as such. In the Discussion the authors state that the study did not detect formal thought disorder or language disorganisation during the conditions tested, apart from modest effects on the alogia subscale of the negative-symptom scale; allowing that their assessments may not have been the most sensitive measures of such symptoms, they add that blocking, loosening of associations and language disorganisation were all noted during the loading doses.

evidence_set: The review reports, second-hand from a study in ten healthy male volunteers, that clearance of S-ketamine was higher when it was given alone (26.3 mL/kg/min) than that of racemic ketamine (14.8 mL/kg/min), and that the clearance of the S-form inside the racemate (18.5 mL/kg/min) was lower than when it was given alone, which the authors read as R-ketamine inhibiting the elimination of S-ketamine; it also states that R-ketamine is not formed after intravenous S-ketamine in humans, so the two forms do not interconvert.
